content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list: 167.15, 143.85, 130.30, 34.53, 34.53, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, maybe 20-30. Here we have three low-field aliphatic: 34.53 (two identical), 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. 34.53 could be a CH2 or CH3 attached to something electron-withdrawing (maybe carbonyl). But typical methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl) ~30 ppm. So 34.53 could be methyl of acetyl. Two identical suggests two equivalent methyls. 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 also could be methyls.

We need to infer the molecule. Let's also get proton NMR to help.
